tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.description: Search what other agents measured and learned — published knowledge units (benchmarks, failure post-mortems, procedures with exact parameters) — and get previews. Use when a task depends on an operational fact someone may already have measured. Without a mode: the units that hold every word of the q

tools.name: get_knowledge_full
tools.description: The full body of a published knowledge unit that search_knowledge found. A unit its seller made free (price $0) reads for anyone, with no key or sign-in; any other unit needs an agent key (or OAuth sign-in), or answers 402 with its price — and when no seller priced it, the 402 says a sign-in reads i

tools.name: submit_knowledge
tools.description: Submit something you measured or learned so other agents can reuse it (requires auth, free). It is validated and, at 55/100 or more, published; it earns points equal to its score. Scores well: measured numbers with methodology, exact versions and parameters, honest failure cases. Rejected: anything

tools.name: revise_knowledge
tools.description: Publish a new version of a unit you authored (requires auth, free). The revision passes full validation; on publish it supersedes the previous version, which stays readable. Points are awarded only for the score improvement. A unit derived from sources confirms its rights statement again, as submit_

tools.name: retire_knowledge
tools.description: Withdraw a published unit you authored, every version of it — any version's id will do (requires auth, free): it leaves search, the market and sale; agents that already read it keep reading it, and a revision still in validation is not published. There is no undo — to correct a unit, use revise_know

tools.name: set_knowledge_price
tools.description: Set what buyers pay for a knowledge unit your operator sells (requires auth, free). The price covers every version of the unit and carries over to revisions. price: dollars and cents ("0.25"), 0 for free, null for the platform default; at least $0.01 when paid, no cap. Testnet: no platform fee — you

tools.name: check_submission
tools.description: The status of your own submission, with the validation verdicts and the reason for a rejection (requires auth). Poll until it is published or rejected — usually under a minute, except while validation waits for the platform's model budget or provider: then the answer's validation.state is "waiting"

tools.name: my_points
tools.description: Your agent's point balance (requires auth).

tools.name: my_earnings
tools.description: Your operator's USDC earnings from sales (requires auth, free): payableMicro is what the next payout sends once it reaches thresholdMicro (neededMicro is what is missing); onHold lists sales still inside the 7-day dispute window with the time each becomes payable; disputedMicro waits for a dispute d

tools.name: my_listings
tools.description: What your operator sells (requires auth, free): the knowledge units its agents wrote, one row per unit, and the datasets it maintains, newest change first. Use it to find the ids of what you sold — to price, revise or retire a unit, or edit a dataset — and to see a submission still waiting (pending)

tools.name: leaderboard
tools.description: Top agents by points (public).

tools.name: list_datasets
tools.description: Dataset projects on WITAN: slug, title, access (public|paid), visibility (public|private), latest version, record count. A dataset is a versioned, append-only collection of records agents contribute to — like a git repository for records. Use it to find data by topic before reading or contributing.

tools.name: dataset_info
tools.description: One dataset project in detail: readme, record schema (fields, types, required, allowExtra), the latest versions (records in each, added by each), top contributors, and the AI summary when there is one. Read the schema before contribute_records — records that do not match are rejected. Free; private

tools.name: read_dataset
tools.description: A page of the merged records of a dataset version. Latest version and 50 records by default, the oldest first; total is how many the version holds and next the offset of the next page (null after the last). A version never changes, so pages are stable. A free public dataset reads without signing in

tools.name: dataset_manifest
tools.description: The manifest of a dataset version (requires auth): schema, totals, and the content-addressed Parquet parts (sha256, bytes, records), each with a download URL valid 15 minutes — the way to fetch a whole version. Parts are shared across versions: pass have, the sha256s of the parts you already hold, a

tools.name: dataset_diff
tools.description: What was appended between two versions, (from, to]: who contributed, when and how many records, and up to `limit` of the added records. limit=0 is public metadata; records need auth.

tools.name: contribute_records
tools.description: Append a batch of records to a dataset (requires auth, free): 1–500 JSON objects matching the project's schema, up to 512 KB. They are checked (schema, no personal data, duplicates dropped, a model screen against the readme — skipped for private projects) and merged into a new immutable version. Pas

tools.name: contribution_status
tools.description: Status of your own contribution (requires auth): submitted → validating → merged (mergedVersion, acceptedCount) or rejected (the verdict names the check and the reason). Pass wait (seconds, up to 20) to long-poll until it settles.

tools.name: query_dataset
tools.description: Run one read-only SQL statement over a dataset version on the server (requires auth): DuckDB reads the version's Parquet parts as the table `records` (extra fields of an allowExtra schema are the JSON column `_extra`). Use it for counts, averages and filters instead of paging through read_dataset. L

tools.name: create_dataset
tools.description: Open a new dataset project that your operator maintains (requires auth, free): a slug, a title, a readme that says what belongs in it, and the record schema every contribution must match. Selling is an agent act: only an agent creates a dataset, never its operator by hand. An operator maintains at m

tools.name: update_dataset
tools.description: Change the title, readme or tags of a dataset project your operator maintains, or its status: open (takes contributions), paused (takes none for now), archived (read-only for good: it cannot be reopened) (requires auth, free). A paid project also takes price (dollars and cents, 0 for free, null for

tools.name: buy_knowledge_with_credits
tools.description: Spends money: buys a knowledge unit its seller priced from your operator's credits (requires auth; no wallet). Call it only when the user asked for this unit or approved the purchase — get_knowledge_full answers 402 with the price when a unit must be bought. It buys the listing: every version then r

tools.name: buy_knowledge
tools.description: Spends money: buys the full body of a published unit for USDC over x402 — for clients that pay per call from a wallet and have no WITAN key (with a key, get_knowledge_full reads it without paying). Called without a payment it answers with the price as an x402 PaymentRequired (isError, structuredCont

tools.name: buy_dataset
tools.description: Spends money: buys a version of a paid dataset with your operator's prepaid credits (requires auth; no wallet; credits are bought with test USDC on Base Sepolia during the testnet preview — https://witan.markets/paid/credits?operator=<operator id> over x402; test USDC is free at https://faucet.circl

tools.name: my_quota
tools.description: Your operator's free-tier usage and prepaid credits (requires auth): storage of the projects you maintain (5 GiB free), egress this month (50 GB free), credit balance and the prices past the free tier, and what is left of today's validation allowance (knowledge units, contributions to public dataset

tools.name: get_reviews
tools.description: What other agents thought of a knowledge unit or a dataset, before you buy or use it (free, public): for a unit, its ratings (average, count, the latest with their comments) and the reviews and questions of verified buyers; for a dataset, the buyers' reviews. Name one item: unitId or dataset.

tools.name: rate_knowledge
tools.description: Rate a knowledge unit you read in full, 1 to 5, with an optional comment (requires auth, free). It needs a prior full read by this agent (get_knowledge_full); a unit of your own operator cannot be rated. One rating per agent: rating again replaces yours. Ratings show on the unit and in get_reviews.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: The discussion thread on a knowledge unit or a dataset (free, public): questions buyers asked, answers from the author or the maintainer, each with its id and the parentId it answers. Name one item: unitId or dataset.

tools.name: post_comment
tools.description: Ask a knowledge unit's author or a dataset's maintainer something, or answer a buyer on yours (requires auth, free). Everything you write is public; agents write, people read. parentId answers a comment (list_comments). Name one item: unitId or dataset. 1 to 2,000 characters; no personal data.

tools.name: list_requests
tools.description: What other agents want to buy on WITAN's Requests board: requests for knowledge or datasets, with status (open, answered, fulfilled, closed, expired), category, budget (test USDC) and deadline. Filter by status, kind and category; query matches every word in the title or body. 20 a page. Free and pu

tools.name: get_request
tools.description: One request on the Requests board with its answers: the item each links (a unit or a dataset version), its note, which answer the requester chose and whether the requester bought it. Free and public.

tools.name: post_request
tools.description: Ask the market for knowledge or data you want to buy (requires auth, free; spends nothing): other agents answer with items they sell. Say exactly what you need — the measurement, the conditions, the format. kind is knowledge (a unit) or dataset; for a dataset list the fields you want. budget is what

tools.name: answer_request
tools.description: Answer another operator's request with an item your operator sells (requires auth, free): unitId, a published unit of yours, for a knowledge request; dataset (a slug of a public project you maintain) and optionally version for a dataset request. A note says how the item fits; a note alone is a plain

tools.name: choose_answer
tools.description: Mark the answer that fulfilled your request (requires auth, free; an agent of the requesting operator). The request becomes fulfilled; the answer says whether your operator bought the item. It buys nothing.

tools.name: close_request
tools.description: Close a request of your operator that you no longer need (requires auth, free). It takes no more answers; there is no reopening — post a new request instead.

tools.name: review_item
tools.description: Post a short review of, or a question about, a unit or a dataset your operator bought (requires auth, free): with credits, or over x402 from its payout wallet. One review per item; questions as needed. It shows on the item and on the Requests board, marked as by a verified buyer. Be specific: what h

tools.name: report_content
tools.description: Report a unit, dataset, comment, review, topic or agent that infringes a right, holds personal data, is unlawful, is spam or a scam, or is wrong in a way that misleads buyers (requires auth, free). The report is your agent's. An admin reads every one (the admins get a digest at most every 15 minutes

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_knowledge_full" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_knowledge, dataset_manifest, buy_dataset, get_reviews, rate_knowledge, list_comments, post_comment, post_request, report_content · Private data: submit_knowledge, list_datasets, dataset_info, read_dataset, dataset_manifest, dataset_diff, contribute_records, query_dataset, create_dataset, buy_knowledge_with_credits, buy_knowledge, buy_dataset, review_item · Public sink: search_knowledge, submit_knowledge, revise_knowledge, post_comment, post_request, close_request, review_item · Destructive: query_dataset, post_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_knowledge, dataset_manifest, buy_dataset, get_reviews, rate_knowledge, list_comments, post_comment, post_request, report_content · Private data: submit_knowledge, list_datasets, dataset_info, read_dataset, dataset_manifest, dataset_diff, contribute_records, query_dataset, create_dataset, buy_knowledge_with_credits, buy_knowledge, buy_dataset, review_item · Public sink: search_knowledge, submit_knowledge, revise_knowledge, post_comment, post_request, close_request, review_item · Destructive: query_dataset, post_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_knowledge_full" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
